description: Statistics for biology, medicine and public health: study design, describing biological and clinical data, probability distributions in health data, estimation and hypothesis testing, regression for continuous, binary and count outcomes, survival analysis and the problem of multiple testing in genomic studies. Every method is computed by hand on small examples, then run on real health datasets with interactive plots and notebooks in the browser, taught to the depth of a strong biostatistics course for computing and health science students.
modelledOn: Kirkwood and Sterne, Essential Medical Statistics
Pagano and Gauvreau, Principles of Biostatistics
Altman, Practical Statistics for Medical Research
outcomes: Choose an appropriate study design for a biological or medical question and identify bias, confounding and sources of error.
Summarise and visualise biological and clinical data and compute measures of disease frequency and association.
Apply probability distributions to model counts, proportions and measurements in health data, and evaluate diagnostic tests.
Estimate parameters with confidence intervals and carry out and interpret hypothesis tests, including power and sample size calculations.
Fit, check and interpret linear, logistic and Poisson regression models and Kaplan-Meier and Cox survival models.
Control error rates when testing many hypotheses and report analyses reproducibly according to reporting guidelines.

units.title: Study design in biology and medicine
topics: Populations, samples and variables; observational and experimental studies
Cross-sectional surveys, case-control and cohort studies; randomised controlled trials, blinding and allocation concealment
Bias, confounding and effect modification; causation and the Bradford Hill considerations
Sampling methods: simple random, stratified, cluster and multistage designs as used in demographic and health surveys
Ethics of research on people: informed consent, ethics committees, the Declaration of Helsinki; CONSORT and STROBE reporting guidelines

units.title: Describing biological data
topics: Types of data: categorical, ordinal, discrete and continuous; data cleaning and missing values
Measures of location and spread; percentiles and growth reference charts for children
Graphs: histograms, box plots, scatter plots, Kaplan-Meier curves, forest plots
Measures of disease frequency: prevalence, incidence rate, cumulative incidence; malaria incidence by district
Measures of association: risk difference, risk ratio, odds ratio, rate ratio

units.title: Probability distributions in health data
topics: Probability rules, conditional probability and Bayes' theorem
Diagnostic tests: sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, likelihood ratios and ROC curves; malaria rapid diagnostic tests against microscopy
Binomial distribution for proportions such as sickle cell trait carriers; Poisson distribution for counts of cases
The normal distribution, standardisation and the central limit theorem; transformations of skewed data
Simulation of sampling distributions in the browser

units.title: Estimation and hypothesis testing
topics: Standard errors and confidence intervals for means, proportions, differences and ratios
Hypothesis tests and p-values; type I and type II errors; statistical versus clinical significance
t-tests, paired tests and their non-parametric counterparts: Wilcoxon and Mann-Whitney
Chi-squared and Fisher's exact tests for contingency tables; McNemar's test
Analysis of variance and post hoc comparisons
Power and sample size calculations for a trial of a new antimalarial

units.title: Regression for health outcomes
topics: Correlation and simple linear regression; least squares, residuals and model checking
Multiple linear regression: adjusting for confounders, interactions, categorical predictors
Logistic regression for binary outcomes; interpreting odds ratios; risk factors for anaemia in pregnancy
Poisson and negative binomial regression for counts and rates; offsets
Model building, collinearity and overfitting; prediction models and their validation
Clustered and repeated measures data in brief: mixed models and generalised estimating equations

units.title: Survival analysis
topics: Time-to-event data, censoring and truncation; survival and hazard functions
Kaplan-Meier estimation and the log-rank test
Cox proportional hazards regression; hazard ratios; checking proportional hazards
Time-varying covariates and competing risks in brief
Survival of patients on antiretroviral therapy or of children with sickle cell disease in a cohort study

units.title: Multiple testing
topics: Why testing many hypotheses inflates false positives; the family-wise error rate
Bonferroni and Holm corrections; false discovery rate and the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure
Genome-wide association studies: significance thresholds, Manhattan and QQ plots, population structure
Differential expression analysis and q-values; subgroup analyses and p-hacking in clinical research

units.title: Bayesian methods and reproducible analysis
topics: Bayesian inference in brief: priors, posteriors and credible intervals for a prevalence estimate
Meta-analysis: fixed and random effects, heterogeneity and forest plots
Reproducible analysis with scripts and notebooks; data protection for health records
Capstone: a complete analysis of a public health dataset with a statistical analysis plan and report

schedule.title: Study designs and sources of bias
schedule.exercise: Read three short study summaries (a district malaria survey, a case-control study of anaemia, a bed-net trial) and classify each design, naming its main bias and one confounder.

tasks.title: Classify 15 variables from a clinic register as categorical, ordinal, discrete or continuous and draw the population-to-sample diagram for a district survey
Simulate a randomised trial of 200 patients with block randomisation in code and check that both arms balance on age and sex
Simulate a cohort where age confounds the link between charcoal cooking and cough, then show the crude and age-adjusted risk ratios differ

schedule.title: Sampling and research ethics
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page sampling plan for a health survey in three regions, justifying stratification and clusters, and list the consent steps for illiterate participants.

tasks.title: Draw simple random samples of 50 households from a list of 500 and compare the sample mean household size with the true value over 20 repeats
Compare stratified and cluster sampling of 40 villages across three regions by coding both and comparing estimate spread over 1000 repeated samples
Audit a described trial against a CONSORT checklist in a notebook, flag five missing items and compute how many of 25 items are reported

schedule.title: Describing health data
schedule.exercise: Take a table of weekly malaria cases by district and write a half-page descriptive summary with one graph and the key measures of frequency and association.

tasks.title: Compute mean, median, standard deviation and quartiles for 30 child weights and plot a box plot and histogram
Calculate prevalence, incidence rate and cumulative incidence of malaria by district from case counts and person-time, then rank districts in a bar chart
Build a 2x2 table from a cohort and compute risk difference, risk ratio and odds ratio; show when the odds ratio overstates the risk ratio

schedule.title: Probability and diagnostic tests
schedule.exercise: Solve a problem set on conditional probability and Bayes theorem, then evaluate a rapid diagnostic test for malaria using microscopy as the reference.

tasks.title: Apply Bayes theorem to compute the probability of disease given a positive test for prevalence 5 percent, and verify with 10000 simulated people
Compute sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV and likelihood ratios from a 2x2 table of RDT against microscopy and plot the ROC curve for five cut-offs
Model the number of sickle cell trait carriers among 20 sampled people with a binomial and weekly case counts with a Poisson; fit and check both against given data

schedule.title: Normal distribution and sampling distributions
schedule.exercise: Explain in a short note why the sample mean is approximately normal even for skewed data, using your own simulation plots as evidence.

tasks.title: Standardise 40 birth weights to z-scores and use the normal curve to find the proportion below 2.5 kg and the 90th percentile
Simulate the sampling distribution of the mean for samples of 5, 30 and 100 from a skewed income distribution and plot all three histograms
Test log and square-root transformations on skewed hospital stay data and choose the one giving the best normal Q-Q plot, justifying with a numerical check

schedule.title: Confidence intervals and hypothesis tests
schedule.exercise: Write up a two-sample comparison of blood pressure between two clinics, stating hypotheses, test choice, p-value, confidence interval and clinical meaning.

tasks.title: Compute the standard error and a 95 percent confidence interval for a sample mean and for a proportion of 60 positives out of 200
Simulate 1000 trials under a true null effect at alpha 0.05 and count type I errors, then repeat with a real effect to estimate type II error
Compare two skewed groups of recovery times with a t-test and Mann-Whitney test, report both p-values and say which test fits and why

schedule.title: Categorical tests, ANOVA and power
schedule.exercise: Plan a trial of a new antimalarial: choose the outcome, test, effect size and required sample size, and write one paragraph defending the numbers.

tasks.title: Test association between bed-net use and malaria in a 2x2 table with chi-squared and Fisher exact tests and explain which applies when counts are small
Run one-way ANOVA on haemoglobin across four regions, follow with Tukey comparisons, and report which pairs differ with adjusted p-values
Compute the sample size per arm for an antimalarial trial at 80 and 90 percent power, then plot power against sample size for three effect sizes

schedule.title: Linear and logistic regression
schedule.exercise: Fit and interpret a logistic model for anaemia in pregnancy with three risk factors, and write the odds ratios in plain language for a midwife.

tasks.title: Fit a least-squares line to 25 pairs of age and systolic pressure, report the slope, R squared and plot the residuals to check assumptions
Fit a multiple regression of birth weight on gestational age, maternal age and a categorical rural indicator, and compare adjusted and crude coefficients
Fit a logistic regression for anaemia in pregnancy, convert coefficients to odds ratios with confidence intervals and check calibration in risk deciles

schedule.title: Count models and model building
schedule.exercise: Choose between a Poisson and negative binomial model for clinic visit counts, and write a short critique of an over-fitted prediction model.

tasks.title: Fit a Poisson model for monthly malaria cases per district with population as an offset and report rate ratios for two covariates
Detect collinearity among five predictors using variance inflation factors, then compare a full model and a reduced model on held-out data
Analyse repeated blood pressure readings on 30 patients with a random-intercept model and compare its standard errors with a naive pooled regression

schedule.title: Survival data and the Cox model
schedule.exercise: Summarise a small survival dataset with a Kaplan-Meier plot, a log-rank test and a Cox model, and explain each result to a clinician.

tasks.title: Mark censored and event times on a timeline for 12 patients and compute the survival probability at each event time by hand
Estimate Kaplan-Meier curves for two treatment arms, plot them with confidence bands and run a log-rank test on the difference
Fit a Cox model with age and sex, report hazard ratios, and test the proportional hazards assumption with Schoenfeld residuals on a dataset where it is violated

schedule.title: Applied survival analysis
schedule.exercise: Write a methods and results paragraph for a cohort of patients on antiretroviral therapy, covering censoring, competing risks and time-varying exposure.

tasks.title: Distinguish death and loss to follow-up as competing events in a small cohort table and compute cumulative incidence for each
Estimate 12-month survival of children with sickle cell disease from cohort data with censoring and compare groups by hydroxyurea use
Reanalyse a cohort with a time-varying covariate (starting treatment mid-follow-up) and show how ignoring it creates immortal time bias

schedule.title: Multiple testing and genomics statistics
schedule.exercise: Explain in a short essay why testing 20 subgroups yields a false finding, and how Bonferroni and Benjamini-Hochberg change the conclusions.

tasks.title: Simulate 100 independent tests of true null hypotheses at alpha 0.05 and count false positives, then compute the family-wise error rate for 20 tests
Apply Bonferroni, Holm and Benjamini-Hochberg corrections to 50 given p-values and compare the number of discoveries from each
Simulate a GWAS on 5000 variants with 5 true signals, draw the Manhattan and QQ plots and apply the 5e-8 threshold to see which signals survive

schedule.title: Bayesian methods, meta-analysis and reproducibility
schedule.exercise: Pool five small studies of a treatment effect, interpret the heterogeneity, and write a data management plan for a health dataset.

tasks.title: Combine a Beta prior with 12 positives out of 80 tests to get a posterior prevalence and plot prior, likelihood and posterior with a 95 percent credible interval
Run fixed and random effects meta-analysis on six study results, draw the forest plot and report I squared heterogeneity
Complete a scripted analysis of a district health dataset with a pre-written analysis plan, rerunnable from raw data to final tables and report
